@@127599737 <h> The LA Times 's owner wants to take the struggling paper public . Will it work ? <p> When the legendary journalist David Halberstam wrote his landmark 1979 book about American journalism , The Powers That Be , he focused on four media organizations : the Washington Post , Time magazine , CBS and the Los Angeles Times . <p> His choice of the LA newspaper made perfect sense . Influential and successful , it was owned by a prominent California family , the Chandlers . The paper had high standards , a raft of Pulitzer prizes , and a hard-charging Washington DC bureau that competed successfully with its east coast rivals . For reporters and editors , the LA Times was a prestigious career destination ; if you got there , you probably stayed . <p> Nearly 50 years later , the Los Angeles Times is much smaller in staff size and circulation size and is losing tens of millions of dollars a year . The beleaguered staff was rocked -- again -- in recent weeks with the news that the owner , the billionaire Patrick Soon-Shiong , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . This would , he said , " democratize " it . <p> He offered few details , though , as he made the announcement on a late-night talkshow during an interview with host Jon Stewart , who was roundly criticized for his softball approach . <p> Certainly , the paper has been through hell over the decades . It endured many years of owners far more focused on profits than on the best interests of the reading public . <p> Roughly a decade ago -- long after the Chandlers had sold the paper -- the Times was part of the laughably named and poorly run " Tronc " chain that was busy diminishing the Chicago Tribune and other journalistic institutions . <p> The staff was shrinking , the hope for profits disappearing and the newsroom 's morale low . <p> Then , salvation seemed to arrive . Soon-Shiong , a former surgeon who made his fortune in pharmaceuticals and biotechnology , bought the paper in 2018 , coming in hot with promises of restoring the paper 's greatness and public mission . <p> Champagne corks popped as the new @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to offer relief from all the drama of recent years . <p> But -- ever so sadly -- those promises have turned out to be mostly hollow , though the paper remains the largest news organization in the American west and has a respected editor in Terry Tang , formerly of the New York Times . Though it has many talented journalists who still churn out important investigations , break news and win major awards , it is drowning in red ink and laid off 20% of its staff last year . No local newspaper has had an easy time since the business model changed so radically 20 years ago with the precipitous loss of print advertising . <p> But those with reasonably enlightened local ownership have fared the best . The LA Times , under Patrick Soon-Shiong , could have been in that enviable category -- but it did n't go that way . <p> The chances of restoring the gleam to this journalistic jewel can only be described as uncertain . @@127603605 <h> The UK 's Palestine recognition pledge makes the return of hostages less likely <p> Earlier this week , Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer announced the UK government will recognise a Palestinian state in September -- unless Israel meets certain conditions , including agreeing to a ceasefire in Gaza . <p> Whilst there were demands , no conditions as such were imposed on Hamas ( nor for that matter on the Palestinian Authority ) . <p> This approach is a sharp departure from convention , which has held until now only to recognise a Palestinian state as part of a negotiated process between the parties resulting in a secure Israel alongside a viable Palestinian state . <p> I am sure that the government 's statement was motivated by a genuine humanitarian impulse in relation to the conflict in Gaza . To introduce the issue of recognition in this context is to add an unnecessary complication . <p> The government 's statement is potentially bad news for the hostages still being held by Hamas . <p> For those who need a reminder : this war was not started by Israel . It began on 7 October 2023 , during the Hamas attacks , which saw more than 1,200 men , women and children violently murdered and hundreds kidnapped . <p> Twenty-one months later , there are still 50 hostages being held in Gaza -- some living , some dead . We know from the testimony of released hostages that they have faced abuse and appalling conditions for the past 21 months . <p> Hamas has no incentive for accepting a deal <p> One would hope that any government intervention would have at its core the desire to ensure that those who survive are reunited with their families , and that the bodies of the deceased are returned to their families for @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ will make this less likely to happen . The government 's statement sets conditions on Israel . The UK says that it will recognise Palestinian statehood unless Israel accepts a ceasefire . However , this means that Hamas has no incentive for accepting a deal . If the road of recognition is to be pursued , at a minimum the government must state unequivocally that recognition will not be forthcoming unless Hamas meets UK demands . <p> While the government 's statement does call on Hamas to " immediately release all the hostages , sign up to an immediate ceasefire , accept that they will play no part in the government of Gaza , and commit to disarmament " , these are not conditions on recognition but rather aspirations . <p> Unless the government decides to redesignate these as conditions , the Hamas leadership will realise that to secure recognition as a state , all they need to do is block any ceasefire deals between now and September . We are also alarmed at some of the rhetoric within the Israeli government and by extremist settler violence in the West Bank . <p> This war continues to take an unbearable toll on both Israelis and Palestinians , and nearly all of them would like to see it end as soon as possible . For example , Somaliland declared unilateral independence from Somalia in 1991 . It 's a pretty typical situation for him to end up in : he caves to pressure and announces something he thinks will calm everyone down , only to find no one is happy with what he has come up with . <p> Former hostages and families of those still held captive by Hamas say the plan rewards the terror group for the 7 October atrocities . It 's an affliction caused by the Something Must Be Done reflex . There are many situations , crises and scandals where everyone agrees that the status quo is untenable and something must be done . In this case , as in many others , there is a huge amount of emotion and political pressure building up to the point that something really must be done urgently . Something is announced , often in haste . <p> The problem is that the " something " that politicians often alight on is not guaranteed to be good policy . It may be one of many " things " that could be done , some of which are less obvious than others . And often , the " something " that does get chosen turns out to be bad policy , with unintended consequences . <p> The best example is the way that dangerous @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ on high-profile breeds rather than the reality that many of our cuddliest and most loved breeds , such as retrievers and dachshunds , can be as reactive and aggressive as bull terriers . The emotional rush to do something clouded the need to ensure that the thing alighted upon would actually work . Years of revisions to that dangerous dog legislation underline that the initial " something " was n't the solution at all . <p> The Leveson Inquiry was another Something Must be Done response to public outrage at the already unlawful practices of phone hacking . The Coalition government set it up as a crisis comms move , to try to quell the anger and show that something was being done , only for it to leave a sour taste in mouths of everyone , including the victims of genuine press intrusion who gave evidence , when its recommendations turned out to be unworkable and its second phase was never commissioned . <p> When MPs voted on the legislation implementing some of the recommendations of the Leveson Inquiry , most of them spoke in the debate about the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ specific thing being proposed . They did the same , as it happens , when the latest assisted dying legislation went through its Commons stages , with Kim Leadbeater arguing that something had to be done to address the current situation , and so MPs should support her bill , even if they were n't fully happy with it . <p> That favouring of something , anything , over the thing that is actually going to work is not a practice to admire in politicians : we elect them to respond to our calls for " something " with a rational and well-scrutinised policy , not an emotional and hastily dashed-off plan . <p> Ministers explaining the Palestine announcement this week inadvertently made clear that they were suffering from the Something Must Be Done reflex . They argued that something had to be done to change the situation . The 130 Labour MPs who signed the letter calling for recognition of a Palestinian state did not want to prolong the hunger and suffering in Gaza . In fact , they were presumably motivated largely by the horrendous images of suffering @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Starmer 's statehood pledge is that the Palestinians will only get their recognition if they continue to suffer . <p> Now , they find themselves defending the principle behind the announcement , rather than the detail of the plan itself , because that was never really considered in the rush to do something . Doubtless when Parliament returns in the autumn , we will be subjected to another pointless debate where the majority of MPs argue about the principles rather than the details of this announcement too . <p> Starmer , of course , should know better : after all , lawyers find their work in the unintended consequences of badly-drafted laws that politicians cooked up when the popular mood demanded that " something must be done " . He has , though , rapidly discovered since entering government that many of the problems he diagnosed in his opponents are quite infectious : he too seems to have succumbed to a bad case of Something Must Be Done .
